items.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 23 at 11:00AM AKDT until September 26 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Water levels on average of 1.5 to 2.5 feet above the
normal highest tide line near Kwigillingok. Southeast winds 35
to 45 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected Thursday. South winds
30 to 40 mph with gusts to 50 mph expected Friday.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast including Kwigillingok and
Kipnuk.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Thursday to 4 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be multiple peaks in water
levels
items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
items.instruction:
A coastal flood warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 2:18PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
We are currently tracking a low that is expected to move through
the southern Bering Sea Thursday through Saturday and which could
approach the coast of the Yukon Delta. While the most likely
storm track south of our area would result in only modest rises in

items.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 12:43PM AKDT until September 26 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Interior Kuskokwim Delta, including Kwethluk, Kasigluk,
Bethel, Napaskiak, Napakiak, Oscarville, and other nearby villages.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rain in combination of persistent high water
levels and storm surge may result in flooding of rivers, creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and
streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings may be
